trial_allocation.allocation_rationale: Baseline model — fixed defaults, no HPO needed.
Random Forest is robust but has a moderate search space (n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_split). 15 trials are sufficient to find a strong configuration without overfitting on 24 features.

XGBoost has a large, complex search space (learning_rate, max_depth, subsample, colsample_bytree, reg_alpha, reg_lambda) and is highly sensitive to hyperparameters. 20 trials ensure adequate exploration to maximize ROC-AUC.
LightGBM is also complex but often converges faster than XGBoost due to its leaf-wise growth. 15 trials provide a good balance between exploration and compute time.
Extra Trees has low sensitivity to hyperparameters compared to boosting models, as it relies on random splits. 5 trials are enough to tune n_estimators and max_depth.

checklist.comment: All five candidate models (logistic regression, random forest, xgboost, lightgbm, extra trees) are well-suited for binary or multiclass classification tasks.
Logistic regression is included as a non-HPO baseline, providing a solid interpretable reference point against which to measure gains from more complex ensemble models.

50 total trials distributed across 4 HPO-enabled models yields approximately 12 trials per model. For high-dimensional hyperparameter spaces (especially XGBoost and LightGBM), this budget may limit thorough exploration.
Stratified k-fold cross-validation is appropriate for classification with 4921 samples, ensuring class distribution is preserved across folds.
Primary metric (ROC-AUC) and evaluation metric (ROC-AUC) are aligned and appropriate for classification.
Favorable sample-to-feature ratio (~205:1) and cross-validation strategy mitigate overfitting risk. Tree-based models with HPO should still use regularization constraints.
50 trials on a dataset of ~5000 samples with 24 features is computationally modest. Tree-based model training at this scale is efficient.
Pipeline specification does not explicitly mention random seed configuration for Optuna TPE sampler or model initialization, which may affect result reproducibility.

non_blocking_risks.message: With 50 trials split across 4 HPO candidates, each model receives roughly 12 trials. XGBoost and LightGBM have large hyperparameter spaces where TPE may need more iterations to converge on optimal regions.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Consider allocating trials proportionally to model complexity, or enable Optuna pruning (e.g., MedianPruner) to reallocate budget from underperforming trials to promising configurations.

non_blocking_risks.message: No information provided about class distribution. While ROC-AUC is relatively robust to imbalance, highly skewed classes could affect model calibration and threshold-dependent downstream usage.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Verify class balance in the dataset. If imbalanced, consider adding class_weight parameters to candidate models or stratified sampling strategies.

non_blocking_risks.message: Absence of explicit seed specification for the TPE sampler and cross-validation splits may lead to non-deterministic results across runs.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Ensure fixed random seeds are set for Optuna sampler initialization, cross-validation fold generation, and model random_state parameters.

future_improvement_suggestions: Consider adding a gradient boosting baseline with default hyperparameters (no HPO) to isolate the contribution of hyperparameter tuning versus model architecture choice.
Evaluate whether feature preprocessing (scaling, encoding) is needed, particularly for logistic regression which is sensitive to feature scales compared to tree-based models.
If the HPO budget remains at 50 trials, consider running a two-phase approach: broad exploration first, then focused refinement on the top 1-2 models with additional trials.
Consider tracking additional metrics beyond ROC-AUC (e.g., precision-recall AUC, F1-score) to provide a more comprehensive evaluation, especially if class imbalance exists.
